filename: Unsupervised classification of absorbing aerosols detected by the Single Particle Soot Photometer.pdf
title: Unsupervised classification of absorbing aerosols detected by the Single Particle Soot Photometer
testbed_rationale: The dataset comprises laboratory instrument time series (SP2 laser-induced incandescence) for single-particle aerosol identification and classification, rather than grid-scale climate model simulation outputs for parameterization development.
pain_points: Laboratory training datasets do not fully generalize to ambient atmospheric aerosols
Dust-like aerosols (mineral dust, coal fly ash, volcanic ash) have high heterogeneity and commonly cause optical detector saturation or signal anomalies
Outliers falling far outside the training distribution can produce unreliable latent embeddings in VAEs
Differences in instrument configuration and detector gains across field campaigns affect transferability of representations
extraction_notes: The paper investigates unsupervised learning (PCA and VAE) to compress raw single-particle SP2 time series into low-dimensional latent spaces (optimal dimension n=3) to differentiate absorbing aerosol classes and quantify aerosol population similarity.
